course.title: Course: MAI/MKI - AI Project / KI Project (WS) (Nierhoff) | moodle.oth-aw.de

faqs.html:
Project 1 (water in a bottle)
- Your model should predict how many grams of water are in each bottle based on a single image
- I will hand out a labeled validation dataset the next weeks
- Final evaluation will be based on a test dataset handed out a couple of days before the deadline
- Please do not finetune your model on the test dataset. On the day of the presentation I will ask you for a live output of your offline model on a few completely new images (neither in test nor validation dataset).
- Do not remove the labels from the bottles
- Go to Hauser (the beverage market next to Lidl) to get replacement bottles. Please return the bottles to me as the university does not refund the deposit :/
- You can also use the balance in the Maker Space (room DC 1.04)

Project 2 (racing car)
- The idea is to use two cameras, one to record your hands holding a virtual steering wheel and the other one to record your feet pressing virtual pedals. If you can do it with one camera, that's fine as well

Project 6 (Niryo robot)
- Do not place the robot near/at the edge of the table!
- The pucks to be pushed will be put on the table in front of Maker Space (room DC 1.04). Each group must only take one puck

Project 7 (Turtlebot)
- Do not place the robot on a table or any other elevated surface!
- I will provide the cubes to be pushed tomorrow (most likely 20.10.). You can pick them on the table in front of the maker space

announcements.author: Thomas Nierhoff
announcements.body:
Dear all,
a few updates for the AI project:- I have uploaded the group meeting schedule to this course, attendance via BBB during your timeslot is mandatory. Please hand in a "ärztliches Attest" later if you cannot attend due to medical reasons. Otherwise I'll deduce points for every absent group meeting.- The additional webcams and extension cables for all groups working on project 2 have arrived. Please pick them up during your first group meeting timeslot (next Monday) if you need them. You can also rely solely on your notebook webcam, but both hands and feet should be tracked, thus one or two additonal external webcams might be helpful. Also get them if you are not sure yet whether you will need them.- I have placed the pucks for all groups working on project 6 on the table in front of the maker space, pick one per group.- I have placed the pylons for all groups working on project 7 on the table in front of the maker space, pick two per group.- I have created a FAQ page in this course with additional information for each project. Check it out regularly as additional infos will be added over time.
Best regards,
Thomas Nierhoff

announcements.author: Thomas Nierhoff
announcements.body:
Dear all,
a few information about the AI projects based on the questions asked after the kickoff meeting:- you need to form teams of 2, use the discussion board in this moodle course whenever necessary to find a partner.- no need to hurry for your team/project selection, it is not "first come, first serve". If there are more teams for a specific project than slots available, I'll toss a coin.- sorry, but the 3 groups for each new project is a fixed requirement. I want to avoid that individual teams reuse old, finished projects. - if you conduct your project with another professor, I'll be out of the loop and you can ignore all the deadlines and requirements imposed by me (no need to find a group partner, no need to fill out the project selection form, no need to submit your project before Jan. 10th.). Just finish your project this semester (because the student office will accept grades for this course only this semester) and the other professor will grade you and submit your grade to the student office. But you still have to register in PRIMUSS for "AI Project"- for project 1, 2, 3 and 6 most likely the main issue won't be training a proper model but obtaining a good dataset
Further information about the projects:- project 1: You will be given 3-5 bottles during the HW handout in two weeks. Then your task is to create a dataset and train an offline model (do not just use some LLM API). For the final evaluation I will fill the same bottles with predefined amounts of water, create a test dataset of e.g. 20 images and send them to you. You tell me how much water is in each bottle and I'll compare it with the ground truth data.- project 2: No, you cannot reuse your sim racing rig from home. The idea is to do gesture detection by holding a virtual steering wheel with both hands and pressing virtual pedals. Similar to the first task you have to create a dataset and train an offline model. For the final evaluation I'll also try your simulator.- project 3: This is kind of an open project and probably one of the more tricky ones. Scrape data from the internet and reason which study courses are the most suitable ones. Please be aware that that the output from one or two LLMs will serve as a baseline. Different to the other projects you'll probably have to write some documentation.- project 4 + 5: Evaluation will be based on your final score in the Kaggle leaderboard after the Kaggle submission deadline has ended. No need to be among the top 10%, but you should be better than the publicly available baselines. Also note that the Kaggle submission deadlines are before January 10th.- project 6: imitation learning: You manually conduct the task (pushing the object) with the Niryo robot while recording the corresponding video stream from the webcam mounted onto the endeffector.  Then the video stream will be the model's input and the robot movement will be the model's output that needs to be trained. Final evaluation will be based on a new, previously unseen path the objects needs to be pushed along.- project 7: The idea is to provide an initial prompt and then use a publicly available LLM via API and an agentic workflow in combination with the robot to iteratively improve the robot's capabilities to push an object towards a specific position (without using SLAM, just the wheel encoders are sufficient). E.g. prompt -> LLM programs the robot -> robot tries to push the object -> LLM doublechecks the rollout (robot sensor readings) and improves code ->robot tries to push the object -> LLM doublechecks the rollout (robot sensor readings) and improves code -> ...
